entities.summary:
Animal husbandry, the practice of breeding and raising domesticated animals for food, fiber, milk, or other products, has been a cornerstone of human civilization since the Neolithic Revolution around 10,000 BCE. This ancient practice originated in the Fertile Crescent, where early farmers domesticated animals such as sheep, goats, and cattle to supplement their meager diets. As agriculture spread throughout the ancient world, animal husbandry became a crucial component of many societies, influencing everything from trade and commerce to art and culture. The invention of the wheel, for example, was closely tied to the development of animal-drawn transportation, which revolutionized the movement of goods and people. Animal husbandry also played a significant role in the growth of cities, as the demand for meat and dairy products led to the establishment of specialized butchers, dairy farmers, and other animal-related industries. From the ancient Sumerians to the medieval Europeans, animal husbandry has been a vital part of human history, shaping the course of civilizations and leaving an indelible mark on the natural world.

The legacy of animal husbandry can be seen in the modern meat and dairy industries, which continue to dominate global food production. However, this legacy also comes with significant environmental and social costs, including deforestation, water pollution, and labor exploitation. As the world grapples with the challenges of sustainability and social justice, it is essential to reexamine the history of animal husbandry and its impact on human societies.
